prs.title: fix: terminate active StreamableHTTP sessions during shutdown
prs.author: weiguangli-io
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: SSE streams (GET/standalone and session-level) are not closed when the StreamableHTTP session manager shuts down, so active EventSourceResponse coroutines get cancelled mid-stream instead of completing gracefully (causing ASGI 'incomplete response' errors/noise on shutdown). (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: SSE streams (GET/standalone and session-level) are not closed when the StreamableHTTP session manager shuts down, so active EventSourceResponse coroutines get cancelled mid-stream instead of completing gracefully (causing ASGI 'incomplete response' errors/noise on shutdown). (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2253's diff makes terminate() actually iterate and close every entry in self._sse_stream_writers, and reorders streamable_http_manager.py's shutdown lifespan to call terminate() before task cancellation — this is the piece that performs the graceful close. #3218 only registers/pops the GET-request stream's writer into self._sse_stream_writers (its own comment says this is so 'session terminate() can close this ASGI response'), i.e. it depends on terminate() already having closing logic. Without #2253's terminate()/lifespan change, #3218 alone does not achieve graceful shutdown. #2253 is the fuller fix; #3218's GET-registration piece would need to be folded into it if anything is missing for the GET stream case.

prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs touch the exact same line in src/mcp/server/stdio.py that constructs the write_stream via create_memory_object_stream/create_context_streams with a hardcoded buffer size of 0, and both are motivated by the same root cause: a zero-size buffer on the write stream causes handler tasks to block when queuing a message (e.g. a final response) while the stdout writer is still flushing an earlier one (e.g. a progress notification). PR #2215 instead adds read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size parameters but leaves both defaults at 0, so the underlying blocking behavior is unchanged unless every caller opts in by explicitly passing a non-zero buffer size — it doesn't fix the reported deadlock by default and has no test covering that scenario. prs.author: ulofiai
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError (and its UrlElicitationRequiredError subclass) is not pickle-safe: the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is (code, message, data) set by MCPError.__init__, which doesn't match subclass constructors like UrlElicitationRequiredError's (elicitations, message) — raising TypeError on unpickle (issue #2431). (3 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: MCPError (and its UrlElicitationRequiredError subclass) is not pickle-safe: the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is (code, message, data) set by MCPError.__init__, which doesn't match subclass constructors like UrlElicitationRequiredError's (elicitations, message) — raising TypeError on unpickle (issue #2431). (3 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #2555 only overrides __reduce__ on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so any other MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor signature remains broken. #2478 and #3262 both fix __reduce__ at the MCPError base class so all subclasses benefit, but #2478's _restore_mcp_error dispatches via from_error_data/from_error and needs a hardcoded special case added for every subclass whose constructor doesn't fit the generic from_error_data mapping (as seen for UrlElicitationRequiredError). #3262 instead uses MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__(*args) plus a __dict__ state payload in the __reduce__ 3-tuple, which restores arbitrary subclass instance attributes without any per-subclass branching. Its test diff also adds a pickle round-trip test against NoBackChannelError (a plain subclass) in addition to UrlElicitationRequiredError, demonstrating the fix generalizes rather than covering only the one reported subclass.

clusters.pick_reason: #2253's diff makes terminate() actually iterate and close every entry in self._sse_stream_writers, and reorders streamable_http_manager.py's shutdown lifespan to call terminate() before task cancellation — this is the piece that performs the graceful close. #3218 only registers/pops the GET-request stream's writer into self._sse_stream_writers (its own comment says this is so 'session terminate() can close this ASGI response'), i.e. it depends on terminate() already having closing logic. clusters.pick_reason: #2555 only overrides __reduce__ on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so any other MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor signature remains broken. #2478 and #3262 both fix __reduce__ at the MCPError base class so all subclasses benefit, but #2478's _restore_mcp_error dispatches via from_error_data/from_error and needs a hardcoded special case added for every subclass whose constructor doesn't fit the generic from_error_data mapping (as seen for UrlElicitationRequiredError). #3262 instead uses MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__(*args) plus a __dict__ state payload in the __reduce__ 3-tuple, which restores arbitrary subclass instance attributes without any per-subclass branching. Its test diff also adds a pickle round-trip test against NoBackChannelError (a plain subclass) in addition to UrlElicitationRequiredError, demonstrating the fix generalizes rather than covering only the one reported subclass.

clusters.pick_reason: 3243 is the only one of the three that also fixes a task-affinity hazard: it replaces context.lock (anyio.Lock) with anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) because httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator on a different task than the one that acquired the lock, which anyio.Lock does not safely support for cross-task release. It further splits out a dedicated flow_lock so refresh/authorization transitions serialize independently from ordinary resource requests, giving finer-grained concurrency than #2858's scope-narrowing or #3252's move-the-yield-outside-the-lock approach, both of which keep anyio.Lock and remain exposed to that cross-task release issue.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys the in-flight map with str(message.id), which collapses JSON-RPC integer id 1 and string id "1" into the same key — causing a false-positive rejection of a legitimate concurrent request, and does not guard against a string id colliding with the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY sentinel. #3221 introduces a type-preserving key helper (`i:`/`s:` prefixes) that keeps int and string ids distinct and explicitly prevents collision with GET_STREAM_KEY, closing both edge cases the simpler #3063 implementation leaves open.

clusters.pick_reason: 3251 is the only PR of the four that fixes both halves of the bug in one place: it recomputes token_expiry_time in _initialize() (the exact fix in #1784) and also restores authorization-server metadata via a getattr-guarded duck-typed lookup that works against existing TokenStorage implementations without changing the interface (covers the same goal as #2492, which instead adds new abstract get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata methods to the TokenStorage Protocol, a larger interface change every implementer must adopt). clusters.pick_reason: #2253's diff makes terminate() actually iterate and close every entry in self._sse_stream_writers, and reorders streamable_http_manager.py's shutdown lifespan to call terminate() before task cancellation — this is the piece that performs the graceful close. #3218 only registers/pops the GET-request stream's writer into self._sse_stream_writers (its own comment says this is so 'session terminate() can close this ASGI response'), i.e. it depends on terminate() already having closing logic. clusters.pick_reason: #2555 only overrides __reduce__ on UrlElicitationRequiredError itself, so any other MCPError subclass with a non-matching constructor signature remains broken. #2478 and #3262 both fix __reduce__ at the MCPError base class so all subclasses benefit, but #2478's _restore_mcp_error dispatches via from_error_data/from_error and needs a hardcoded special case added for every subclass whose constructor doesn't fit the generic from_error_data mapping (as seen for UrlElicitationRequiredError). #3262 instead uses MCPError.__new__ + Exception.__init__(*args) plus a __dict__ state payload in the __reduce__ 3-tuple, which restores arbitrary subclass instance attributes without any per-subclass branching. Its test diff also adds a pickle round-trip test against NoBackChannelError (a plain subclass) in addition to UrlElicitationRequiredError, demonstrating the fix generalizes rather than covering only the one reported subclass.

members.author: MukundaKatta
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3262: MCPError (and its UrlElicitationRequiredError subclass) is not pickle-safe: the default Exception.__reduce_ex__ reconstructs via cls(*self.args), but self.args is (code, message, data) set by MCPError.__init__, which doesn't match subclass constructors like UrlElicitationRequiredError's (elicitations, message) — raising TypeError on unpickle (issue #2431).

clusters.pick_reason: 3243 is the only one of the three that also fixes a task-affinity hazard: it replaces context.lock (anyio.Lock) with anyio.Semaphore(1, max_value=1) because httpx can resume or close the auth-flow generator on a different task than the one that acquired the lock, which anyio.Lock does not safely support for cross-task release. It further splits out a dedicated flow_lock so refresh/authorization transitions serialize independently from ordinary resource requests, giving finer-grained concurrency than #2858's scope-narrowing or #3252's move-the-yield-outside-the-lock approach, both of which keep anyio.Lock and remain exposed to that cross-task release issue.

clusters.pick_reason: #3063 keys the in-flight map with str(message.id), which collapses JSON-RPC integer id 1 and string id "1" into the same key — causing a false-positive rejection of a legitimate concurrent request, and does not guard against a string id colliding with the reserved GET_STREAM_KEY sentinel. #3221 introduces a type-preserving key helper (`i:`/`s:` prefixes) that keeps int and string ids distinct and explicitly prevents collision with GET_STREAM_KEY, closing both edge cases the simpler #3063 implementation leaves open.

members.title: fix(streamable-http): reject duplicate in-flight request ids
members.author: Sammy-Dabbas
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #3221: Both fix the same bug: `_request_streams` is keyed by request id, so a second concurrent request reusing the same id silently overwrites the first's routing slot, cross-wiring responses (one request gets the other's payload, the other hangs). Both add a rejection (HTTP 409/400) for duplicate in-flight request ids.
